decisions.what: Set plugin/pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds '@ast-grep/cli' to false (explicit deny), not true.
decisions.why: @ast-grep/cli ships a JS bin shim whose postinstall replaces it with the native binary. pnpm generated a `node`-invoking .bin shim (the original target had a node shebang), so after the postinstall swap `pnpm exec ast-grep` runs `node <ELF>` and fails with SyntaxError. Denying the build keeps the JS fallback shim, which spawns the platform optional binary at runtime; this is the only state where `pnpm install` exits 0 AND `pnpm exec ast-grep` runs. Cost: a benign stderr warning from the fallback, which the runner ignores for coverage state.

decisions.what: Rewrote normalizeKnipJson to read knip 6's `{issues:[{files,exports,dependencies}]}` schema instead of the legacy flat `{files,exports,dependencies}` string arrays.
decisions.why: The installed knip is 6.25.0, which only emits the issues[] shape; the legacy parser silently produced zero findings, so knip coverage was restored in name only. The new parser maps issue.files->unused_file, issue.exports->unused_export (with line), issue.dependencies->unused_dependency, all as MAINT-003 review_required deletion candidates. Updated knip.test.ts to the knip 6 shape.

decisions.what: Set plugin/.jscpd.json `threshold` to 100 (report-only) instead of 0.
decisions.why: With threshold 0 jscpd exits 1 ("too many duplicates over threshold") on any duplication, which reads as an error even though the report file is still written. threshold 100 makes jscpd exit 0 while still emitting every duplicate into jscpd-report.json; the adapter's report-file parse is the real gate (valid report -> run/findings, missing report -> failed/degraded), so signal is preserved and the exit code stays clean.

decisions.what: Placed sgconfig.yml at the repo root with `ruleDirs: [slop-rules]` and did not add a `--config` flag to the ast-grep command.
decisions.why: Verified empirically that `ast-grep scan` discovers sgconfig.yml by walking up from the absolute target's ancestry, so with cwd=packageRoot (plugin) it still finds the root config and ruleDirs resolve relative to the root. Keeping the command as `pnpm exec ast-grep scan --json=compact <absTarget>` stays minimal and robust. Added one bounded, low-noise rule (no-debugger-statement) so `scan` has a valid rule set and never errors on missing rules.

decisions.what: Added an optional `runner?: ToolRunner` to SlopScanOptions, defaulting to createToolRunner().
decisions.why: runSlopScan previously hardcoded createToolRunner(), making packageRoot-cwd routing and degraded-to-run recovery untestable without spawning real binaries. The seam lets scan.test.ts inject a fake runner that records per-detector cwd/command and flips a detector between unavailable and success, proving required coverage recovers to run purely from tool availability. It is a minimal, additive test seam and does not touch the change.ts hotspot.

follow_ups: Upstream wart to revisit: if pnpm ever regenerates the @ast-grep/cli .bin shim to exec the native binary directly (or @ast-grep/cli stops swapping the bin in postinstall), the allowBuilds '@ast-grep/cli': false override can be flipped to true to remove the benign per-invocation stderr fallback warning. No action required now.

Python (radon/vulture) and Go (gocyclo/go-deadcode) detectors intentionally remain on repoRoot cwd because they are system-installed binaries, not plugin-local node_modules tools, so there is no same-pattern defect to fix there. This is a partially-completed prior extraction — the highest-value, lowest-risk convergence available. Secondary: the withTargetPathStore/withOptionalTargetPathStore dual-path closure pattern repeats at every mutation tool but is spec-anchored (rq-cacheRefresh01, rq-crossProjectTaskMutation01) and already thin; consolidating it risks obscuring the exact target-store routing the specs require, so it is design-around rather than auto-adopt. The change.ts dynamic imports around recovery are intentional workflow-bundle-boundary avoidance (recovery-probe.ts docstring explains recovery-classification is transitively in the workflow bundle), so extraction must preserve tool-layer placement and not hoist probe logic into temporal/.

validation.notes: No spec/security/release blockers. All surfaced candidates are behavior-preserving and have in-repo tested precedents. #65/#192 open-state taken from briefing durable_facts (live gh verification skipped: adv_run_test requires a real task ID and this draft change has none yet).

Consolidating the target_path dual-wrapper would shrink change/task/gate but risks obscuring the spec-mandated target-store cache-refresh routing; keeping it explicit is safer even if more verbose.

change.ts uses dynamic imports deliberately to stay out of the Temporal workflow bundle; a naive static-import refactor could reintroduce the workflow-bundle-boundary regression class the boundary tests guard against.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The re-entry addendum design is architecturally correct and self-consistent with the existing ADV gate state machine. Sequential gate ordering is enforced structurally in three layers: (1) priorGateBlockers computes PRIOR_GATE_INCOMPLETE for any non-done prior gate (gate-readiness.ts:68-85), (2) evaluateGateReadiness surfaces it as a hard blocker (gate-readiness.ts:804), and (3) completeGateWithReadiness marks the gate 'stuck' rather than 'done' when not ready (workflows.ts:958-961). This is the intended state-machine invariant (rq-gatemodel01 sequential enforcement), and an existing test at workflows.signal-handlers.test.ts:852-880 already codifies exactly this rejection behavior for a direct out-of-order design completion. The concurrent-signaling itest is the party at fault: it fires the three DEPENDENT gate completions (proposal->discovery->design) inside a concurrent Promise.allSettled burst (itest:170-184, 301-317) whose processing order is nondeterministic. gateCompletionChain (workflows.ts:1204,1353-1357) serializes signal handlers but does not impose dependency ordering; therefore design or discovery can be processed before proposal is done, land in 'stuck', and never self-heal (change-state.ts:1143-1166 has no buffer/retry). The design's preferred fix -- sequence the three dependent gate completions with barriers, keep the remaining independent signal burst concurrent, and change product code only under a focused RED proof -- preserves the invariant, matches the boring/proven approach, and restores deterministic stress coverage. It is strictly preferable to weakening workflow readiness (buffering/auto-retrying arbitrary future gate completions), which would erode the state machine and mask real out-of-order-completion bugs.

# Optimize adapter surfaces

## Why

ADV adapter/tool surfaces are harder to evolve safely because change, task, and tool-registry concerns are coupled across large implementation hot spots. Schema validation, target-path routing, Temporal signal dispatch/cache refresh, recovery handling, and response formatting are not consistently isolated. This raises regression risk for Temporal-backed state mutation, cross-project `target_path` behavior, typed tool boundaries, and future performance/structure work in the optimizeAdvPerformanceStructure Epic.

Discovery clarification expanded the intended outcome: optimize primarily for clearer maintainable boundaries, include verification/fix of the open #192-style `target_path` readback/close routing behavior where current code or tests still drift, and allow response-envelope cleanup when design proves it is safer and backward-compatible enough.

## What Changes

This change proposes adapter-surface optimization with bounded functional repair:

- Identify the highest-coupling seams in change/task/tool-registry adapter code.
- Separate schema-boundary validation, target-path routing, signal/cache-refresh helpers, recovery handling, and formatter/projection concerns where evidence shows extraction reduces risk.
- Preserve existing tool contracts and Temporal signal/query behavior with deterministic tests unless design proves a safer additive/cleanup response shape.
- Verify #192-style `target_path` readback/update/close routing behavior against current code and tests; fix remaining drift in scope.
- Consider issue #65 only where it directly matches schema-boundary validation or typed tool argument handling.
- Keep changes scoped to adapter-surface structure and target-path routing correctness, not broad feature redesign.

## User Outcomes

- ADV maintainers can change task/change/tool behavior with less risk of unrelated adapter regressions.
- Tool contract behavior remains stable or improves through intentional, tested cleanup rather than incidental drift.
- Cross-project `target_path` readback/update/close operations are verified or corrected so source-project sessions do not silently use wrong project identity or non-authoritative artifact content.
- Future Epic performance/structure work has smaller, clearer surfaces to build on.

## Affected Code

Likely areas for discovery/design validation:

- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` — large change-tool surface with artifact readback, update, close/bulk close, recovery, archive, origin, and formatting.
- `plugin/src/tools/target-project.ts` — `withTargetPathStore`, `withOptionalTargetPathStore`, and target project context/authority formatting.
- `plugin/src/tools/_adapters.ts` — signal/cache refresh, handle/reachability adapter helpers.
- `plugin/src/tools/task.ts` — task mutation routing, target-path handling, task status lifecycle.
- `plugin/src/tools/gate.ts` — gate mutation routing and target-path signal path.
- `plugin/src/tool-registry.ts` and `plugin/src/utils/tool-arg-preflight.ts` — tool schema/preflight boundaries.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/change/artifacts.ts` — Temporal document/artifact content readback and update behavior.
- Nearby tests under `plugin/src/tools/*.test.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/change.read-artifact.test.ts`, target-project tests, and boundary/spec drift tests where applicable.

## Related Repositories

- Current repo only: `/home/jon/dev/advance`.
- No product-linked cross-repo implementation scope identified.
- Cross-project behavior must be represented via temp/test target projects, not live external repo mutation unless explicitly approved later.

## Constraints

- Specs are law: implementation must preserve relevant requirements in `advance-delivery`, `advance-workflow`, `advance-meta`, and cross-project coordination requirements.
- Preserve Temporal signal/query model; do not introduce update-based mutation surfaces.
- Preserve `fireSignalAndRefresh` cache-refresh discipline for change-workflow signals.
- Preserve `withTargetPathStore(...)` target-store routing for cross-project mutations.
- Preserve snapshot-ok read-only semantics and non-authoritative disk-snapshot markers.
- Preserve tool arg schema/preflight behavior and Zod v4 schema source of truth.
- Preserve root CLI/source-boundary contracts; do not reintroduce forbidden deep imports.
- Do not read or couple to ADV external state files directly.

## Impact

Expected impact is maintainability and regression-risk reduction, plus correction or closure of target-path routing/readback drift if tests confirm current behavior still fails. User-visible behavior may change only through intentional, documented, test-backed cleanup or additive diagnostics.
